'''Maurice De Shawn Taylor''' (born October 30, 1976) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] positions. Originally from [[Detroit]], Taylor played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] and was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] as the 14th overall pick in the [[1997 NBA draft]]. Taylor played from 1997 to 2007 in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] for the Clippers, [[Houston Rockets]], [[New York Knicks]], and [[Sacramento Kings]]. From 2009 to 2011, Taylor played internationally in Italy and China.

==College career==
Taylor attended the [[University of Michigan]]. The athletic forward, from Henry Ford High School in [[Detroit, Michigan|Detroit]], burst onto the national scene during the 1994 [[Maui Invitational Tournament|Maui Invitational]] with fellow freshman [[Maceo Baston]]. He won [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman of the Year for the 1994–1995 season, averaging 12.4 points and 5.1 rebounds and playing in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 14 points and 7 rebounds and was picked 2nd Team All-Big Ten. Off the court that year, Taylor was involved in a traffic accident while out with potential recruit [[Mateen Cleaves]] that left teammate [[Robert Traylor]] with a broken arm and that led to the [[University of Michigan basketball scandal]]. After considering entering the [[NBA draft]], Taylor returned to help lead a talented (if underachieving) Michigan team to the 1997 [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] Championship while averaging 12.3 points and 6.2 rebounds.

==Professional career==

===NBA===

In [[1997 NBA draft|1997]], he was [[NBA draft|draft]]ed 14th overall by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. In 2000, Taylor told the Clippers he would not re-sign with them in free agency or accept any sign-and-trade situations. When he became a free agent, Taylor announced his intention of hoping to sign with the [[Orlando Magic]] to join newly acquired players [[Grant Hill]] and [[Tracy McGrady]].  No contract offer from Orlando ever came. He then signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] instead.  He was then traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in 2005, before joining the [[Sacramento Kings]] in 2006. He was released on January 23, 2007.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-kings-taylor&prov=ap&type=lgns Yahoo! Sports - Sports News, Scores, Rumors, Fantasy Games, and more<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

===Europe===

In January 2009, he joined the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian]] [[Euroleague]] club [[Olimpia Milano]].<ref name=euroleague>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/42852/180/milano-adds-price-for-top-16 Euroleague.net AJ Milano upgrades with Price, Taylor]</ref><ref>[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/56839/20090126/maurice_taylor_signs_three_year_deal_with_milan/ Maurice Taylor Signs Three-Year Deal With Milan] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090203115640/http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/56839/20090126/maurice_taylor_signs_three_year_deal_with_milan |date=2009-02-03 }}</ref>  He had not played since January 2007.<ref name=euroleague/> In February 2011 he signed with [[New Basket Brindisi|Enel Brindisi]] until the end of the season,<ref>[http://www.newbasketbrindisi.it/nbb/portale/news/1311/maurice-taylor-firma-per-l-enel-basket-brindisi Maurice Taylor firma per l'Enel Basket Brindisi] {{in lang|it}}</ref> but reached a consensual termination of the contract with the club in April 2011.<ref>[https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=it&tl=en&u=http://www.newbasketbrindisi.it/nbb/portale/news/1540/comunicato-stampa Comunicato su Taylor] {{in lang|it}}</ref>

==Booster scandal==
{{see also|University of Michigan basketball scandal}}

Years after the completion of his college career, Taylor, along with several other Michigan stars, was accused of taking money from booster Ed Martin.  Due to concerns that Taylor's amateur status had been compromised, Michigan forfeited every game in which Taylor played, and scrubbed his records from its record books.  The school was also forced to disassociate itself from Taylor until 2012.

However, he was in the stands in New York with another former Wolverine, [[Jalen Rose]], to support the team during the 2006 [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] Final Four.

==Personal==
Through his mother, Taylor is of Italian descent.<ref>[http://web.legabasket.it/news/?id=103600 L'Armani Jeans Milano ha tesserato Maurice Taylor] {{in lang|it}}</ref>
